scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Unlimited bandwidth

scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Brand assets
statement: Brand assets You can add and manage your brand assets such as your logo, brand colors, and slogan.
scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Fraud analysis
statement: Fraud analysis When you use Shopify Payments, you automatically get a built-in fraud analysis feature. This feature flags orders that are potentially fraudulent and brings them to your attention to help you avoid chargebacks and losses.
scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Manual order creation
statement: Manual order creation You can create new orders and enter payment details right from your Shopify admin.
scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Discount codes
statement: Discount codes You can offer discount codes and the option for combining discounts to expand your customer base.
scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Custom pricing by market
statement: Custom pricing by market You can set product prices and percentage price adjustments for specific countries or regions. Showing prices in local currencies and setting manual exchange rates is available to stores using Shopify Payments.
scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Abandoned cart recovery
statement: Abandoned cart recovery Abandoned checkout recovery sends automatic emails to customers who leave your store without completing the checkout process. You can customize the email that is sent to customers who leave your store.
scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Analytics
statement: Analytics All plan levels offer the Analytics page, which highlights key analytics, including sales, orders, and online store visitor data.
scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

identifier: Features on all plans, table row Finance reports
statement: Finance reports You can view key financial information about your business by using your finance reports. You can use the finances summary to review an overview of your sales, payments, and pending sales data, or view the full finance reports to get more details.
scope: All the Shopify plans listed on the Pricing and Plans page

The Agentic plan is for merchants that don't already use Shopify as their ecommerce platform. This plan lets you add your products to Shopify Catalog and sell them with Shopify agentic storefronts, without needing to have a Shopify online store or migrate from your existing commerce platform.
The Agentic plan has no monthly subscription fee.

identifier: Shopify for enterprise, Ways to build
statement: Enterprise businesses can use Shopify's full platform or modular components.

identifier: Modular components, table row Shop Pay

identifier: Modular components, table row Storefront component

You can use apps to enhance your Shopify admin or add new features. Apps can either be public or custom.
There are two types of public apps: listed and unlisted. Both undergo Shopify's app review process and can be installed from the Shopify App Store.
Most app charges are billed through Shopify and display on your Shopify bill. However, some third-party apps charge you directly outside of Shopify.
The Built for Shopify badge displays on app listings that have passed Shopify's rigorous testing and meet our highest quality standards.
If an app stops meeting these requirements, then it loses the Built for Shopify status. Shopify reviews certifications annually to maintain quality standards.
A custom app is an app that you or a developer builds exclusively for your Shopify store, unlike a public app that's built for many stores to use.
You create and manage custom apps using the Dev Dashboard.
To access Custom Level 2 PII apps, your store must be on the Grow plan or higher.

New versions of Shopify APIs are released every three months. These versions can introduce new features or change and remove existing features. Each version of a Shopify API continues to work for a year before app developers must update their apps to use a newer version.
An app becomes unsupported if the app's developers don't keep it up to date with changes to Shopify's APIs.
Some apps add features to your store using extensions and functions. Extensions and functions are set up by the app developer and become available when you install and activate the app.
Extensions allow apps to add functionality to areas such as your Online Store, checkout, customer accounts, or Point of Sale.
Functions allow apps to customize your store's backend logic.
You activate and deactivate extensions and functions in the area of your Shopify admin where they're used.

Expansion stores are additional .myshopify.com stores that fall under the same organization and contract on your Shopify Plus plan. This allows you to create separate stores, each with their own unique store settings, configurations, and storefronts, and maintain centralized organization-level management for users and billing.
scope: Shopify Plus plan

identifier: Considerations for expansion stores on the Shopify Plus plan
statement: Store settings, products, collections, and inventory aren't synced between stores. They don't share data by default.

identifier: Considerations for expansion stores on the Shopify Plus plan
statement: Apps are billed on a per-store basis rather than for the entire organization.

identifier: Considerations for expansion stores on the Shopify Plus plan
statement: Theme licenses are required for each individual store, and a license can't be shared across stores.

Shopify Plus plan organizations can have a maximum of ten stores on their contract with no additional cost: * One main store. * Nine expansion stores. * Staging stores don't count towards the ten store limit.
Dev stores can use feature previews, demo data, and app development features, but can't process transactions.

identifier: About Shopify API versioning, Release schedule
statement: Each stable version is supported for a minimum of 12 months, with at least nine months of overlap between consecutive versions.

identifier: About Shopify API versioning, version types
statement: Shopify supports three version types:

identifier: About Shopify API versioning, version types
statement: * Stable: Recommended for production. Guaranteed not to change for its supported lifetime. * Release candidate: Published on the same date as the stable release. For example, when 2026-04 releases on April 1, 2026, the 2026-07 release candidate also becomes available. May include backwards-incompatible changes, so not recommended for production. * Unstable: Updated continuously with in-progress changes. Features can be added or removed at any time with no guarantee of release. Use it for early testing only.
When part of a Shopify API becomes unnecessary, unsafe, or outdated, it's deprecated across all supported stable versions and announced in the developer changelog with migration guidance.
If your app continues to use unsupported resources after the upgrade deadline, it's delisted from the Shopify App Store.

Shopify's feature previews give you early access to changes to Shopify so that you can build on the platform with confidence. You can test features that'll be available to users in the upcoming months, but that haven't yet been rolled out.
When a new feature is accompanied by a backwards-incompatible change to our APIs, or a significant change to the online store or the Shopify admin, it's included in a feature preview.
To use a feature preview, specify it when you create a dev store. Only one feature preview may be enabled on a dev store.
Increased variants extended_variants Raises the number of variants that a product can have. Themes that assume a complete variant list need updating first. Refer to Support high-variant products.

Liquid July 2026 changes liquid_july_26_changes Adds the {% block %} and {% partial %} Liquid tags, so you can compose storefront pages in Liquid instead of JSON and refresh part of a page without a full reload.

Market-driven shipping market_driven_shipping Moves shipping configuration into Markets, so merchants manage where they sell and how they ship in the same place. Refer to Feature preview for market-driven shipping.
Physical inventory physical_inventory_apis Adds bins, counts, and purchase orders to the unstable GraphQL Admin API. Refer to Feature preview: Physical inventory.

Ship and pickup in one order ship_and_pickup_in_one_order Lets a buyer ship some items and pick up others in a single order. Available to Shopify Plus merchants. Refer to About split carts in checkout.

Shopify admin's new design new_admin_design Applies the new visual design to the Shopify admin so you can check how your app's App Home surfaces look before merchants get the design. Refer to App Home.

When a stable API version introduces a backwards-incompatible change, the feature associated with the change won't be available to a user's Shopify admin until nine months later, when that version of the API is the oldest supported stable version.
An app extension isn't an app. It's a mechanism that lets an app add features to certain defined parts of several Shopify user interfaces.
Extension-only apps can only be installed with custom distribution.
Your app configuration and all extensions are versioned together as a single app version.
Some app extensions need to be reviewed and approved before they're released to users.
The following table lists all of the available app extensions that you can build.

identifier: List of app extensions, Admin blocks

identifier: List of app extensions, App Home UI extensions
statement: App Home App Home UI extensions No Build a Shopify-hosted landing page for your app in the admin, with no backend required.

identifier: List of app extensions, Checkout UI extensions
statement: Checkout Checkout UI extensions No Add custom workflows and functionality at defined points in the checkout process.

identifier: List of app extensions, Shopify Functions
statement: Shopify Functions No Inject custom code into key areas of the Shopify platform, such as checkout or cart.
Post-purchase Yes Help users increase sales by adding products for purchase after checkout.

identifier: List of app extensions, Customer account UI extensions
statement: Customer accounts Customer account UI extensions No Add functionality at defined points in customer accounts.
Templates Yes Create an example workflow that's available in Flow's template library and can be copied into a merchant's store.

identifier: List of app extensions, Payments extension
statement: Payments Payments extension Yes Allow customers to complete purchases using a payment method provided by your app.

identifier: List of app extensions, POS UI extensions
statement: Shopify Point of Sale (POS) POS UI extensions No Add custom functionality at defined areas in the POS app.
